title: Vectors: representations, coordinates, and the basics of addition and scaling
summary: This video introduces the vector as a foundational concept in linear algebra, exploring three related perspectives (physics, computer science, and mathematics) and emphasizing the origin-centered geometric view. It explains how vectors can be seen as arrows in space or as ordered lists of numbers, and it shows how a vector in 2D is represented by coordinates (x, y) anchored at the origin, with a brief extension to 3D. The core operations—vector addition (via the tip-to-tail method) and scalar multiplication (scaling)—are defined and illustrated, including how coordinates transform under these operations. The video also discusses the intuition behind these operations, why they are defined the way they are, and how the two representations (space-and-geometry versus numerical lists) interrelate. It ends by foreshadowing more advanced topics like spans, bases, and linear dependence in subsequent videos.

sections.title: What is a vector? Perspectives and the origin
concepts: physics perspective: arrows with length and direction
computer science perspective: ordered lists of numbers
sections.description: Sets up three viewpoints on vectors (physics, CS, math) and emphasizes that in linear algebra vectors are typically rooted at the origin, with a geometric intuition tied to arrows in space and a numerical representation as coordinate lists.

sections.title: Coordinate systems and the origin
sections.description: Explicitly walks through the 2D coordinate system, defines the origin as the center, and explains how coordinates tell you how far to move along axes to reach a vector's tip, with a note on extending to three dimensions.

sections.title: Vector representation and placement
sections.description: Links the geometric arrow view to the numerical coordinate view, clarifying that a vector is determined by the coordinates of its tip from the origin and how those coordinates encode the vector.

sections.title: Numerical example of vector addition (tip-to-tail)
concepts: sum as a vector from the original tail to the final tip
sections.description: Demonstrates how to add two vectors by placing the tail of the second at the tip of the first and drawing the resultant from the first tail to the second tip.

sections.title: Scaling vectors: scalar multiplication
sections.description: Explains that multiplying a vector by a scalar scales its length and can flip direction when the scalar is negative, emphasizing that scalars multiply each component of the vector.
